1.21.1.0.630.0:
### 0.630.0

**Find the books you wrote, even the ones the train hasn't let out**

Your own library rooms now stock the books you wrote that the train is still deciding about — or has decided against. Open one and its last page tells you where it stands, in the train's own words. You can also take one of your released books back out of circulation whenever you like.

- Books you wrote that are pending, undecided or refused now appear on your own library shelves instead of vanishing the moment you sign them.
- The last page of one of your books says where it stands: still being read, undecided, or turned away — in orange, or red once it is a no.
- Made Private: take one of your released books off the line so only you can find it. Reversible — the padlock shows what it will do before you click it.
- Protest a verdict you disagree with, on a book the train has actually read. It asks a person to look again; it does not overturn anything by itself.
- No thumbs on a book you wrote — rating your own work was never the point, and it skewed which books everyone else was shown.

### 0.629.0

**Changed settings now show at launch, with one-click restore**

Dungeon Train's difficulty settings are what your advancements and lifetime stats are measured against, so a world running with them changed now plays in Free Play — the same rule that already applied to Adventure Item Stats. If your settings differ, the game tells you on the title screen, lists exactly what changed, and offers to put them back. Your own settings are always backed up first, never deleted, so you can rename a file back to restore them. Settings that don't affect balance — visual options, Discord and telemetry toggles, and the content filters — are unaffected.

- Changed difficulty settings are shown at launch, not discovered mid-run
- One-click restore to defaults, with your old settings kept as backups
- Keeping your changes is remembered, so you're only asked again if something else changes
- New /fixconfig command does the same restore from in-game
1.21.1.0.628.0:
### 0.628.0

**Flag a cheat mod from the death screen**

The Mod Recommendations page now works both ways. Alongside recommending a mod to the creator, each of your installed mods carries a small warning icon — click it to flag that mod as a cheat or hack, say what it lets you do, and send. Flagged mods sink to the bottom of the grid with a warning mark, the way recommended ones keep their tick.

- Report any installed mod as a cheat or hack, with a reason
- Recommendations are unchanged — the tile body still recommends
1.21.1.0.627.0:
### 0.627.0

**Endless portal rooms no longer vanish under other players**

In multiplayer, the endless portal rooms only followed one player — usually the host. Anyone else could watch the floor disappear from around them and drop out of the world, and the room stopped growing ahead of them. Every player in the room now gets their own window of rooms.

- The floor around you is never cleared while you are standing near it, whoever else is in the room
- The room keeps building ahead of every player exploring it, not just the first one in
- Extra corridors are held open the same way, so the way back does not disappear behind you

### 0.626.0

**Version number now shown on the pause menu**

The Dungeon Train version line that sits in the corner of the main menu now also appears on the pause menu, so you can check which build you are on without leaving your run. It carries the same update notice as the title screen — if a newer release is out, the line turns amber and clicking it opens the download page for wherever you installed the mod.

- Version number added to the pause (Esc) menu, matching the main menu
- Shows the same clickable 'update available' notice as the title screen
- Visible in multiplayer as well as singleplayer
1.21.1.0.625.0:
### 0.625.0

**Dimensional carriages can stand under their own sky**

A dimensional carriage's template now chooses the sky it stands under — ordinary daylight, daylight that follows the world clock, or a Nether or End cast. The light eases in as you step inside and eases back out as you leave for the corridor home. The mini-world carriage is the first to use it.

- The mini-world dimensional carriage is now daylit
- Room builders get a Sky control in the dimensional carriage editor
- Turn it off server-wide with the new portalRoomDaylight setting

### 0.624.0

**Edible backpacks are findable again**

Edible backpacks turn up in loot chests, iron/gold chests, decorated pots and the starter chest at their original rates again.

### 0.622.0

**Sable updated to 2.0.5**

Dungeon Train now runs on Sable 2.0.5, which fixes several upstream crashes — most notably a panic when you close the CurseForge or Modrinth launcher before entering a world. Sable is a required download, so update it too.

- Fixes the crash from closing the launcher before joining a world
- Requires Sable 2.0.5 — the modpack updates it for you

**Carriages no longer shift when their blocks change**

Blowing up or mining blocks on a carriage could shove the whole carriage sideways, and the shift survived a save and reload. Beds in the Nether and End were the loudest case, but creepers, trap TNT and ordinary mining did it too.

**Endless plains can have a different floor and roof**

A repeating plain's floor and roof are now set separately in the editor, and either one can be air.

**The deserter's hall by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise**

A new portal room behind house doors: a spruce hall built by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise, with the deserter's journal still inside.

- Built by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise

### 0.621.0

**Undo and redo in the train editor**

The in-world editor now has an undo history on Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (Cmd+Z / Cmd+Y on Mac), with an Undo | Redo row in the editor's X menu. It covers block edits, whole-plot actions like Clear and Reset, block variants, and menu changes such as weights, stage links, loot tables and part assignments. Undo works from anywhere — change something, walk away, and you can still take it back.

- Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Y, rebindable from the vanilla Controls screen
- Blocks, whole-plot Clear and Reset, block variants, and menu changes all undo
- A mirrored edit undoes as one step, not one per reflected cell
- Broken containers come back with their contents intact
- Works from anywhere, not just while standing in the plot

### 0.620.0

**JEI, ready to switch on**

The modpack now ships Just Enough Items, off by default. Tick it on at install for recipe and item lookup — press R on any item to see how it's made.

- Bundled with the modpack, switched off by default.
1.21.1.0.619.0:
### 0.619.0

**Three weeks of new text, now in all 19 languages**

Everything added since early August was English-only outside en_us — the seven new advancements, the Video Tools page, the skybox blocks, the difficulty-change warning, the drifting-carriage death lines, the community-book report button and more. All of it is now translated into every language Dungeon Train ships in, along with ten in-world books that had never been localized. Machine-translated and marked as such, so the in-game translation editor lists them for human review.

- 115 newly translated interface lines in each of the 19 languages
- Ten new books — including The Drifting Carriages and the cursed and loved starting books — now read in your language
- New Quiet Rules and Train Glossary entries translated to match the English originals

### 0.618.0

**CurseForge modpack keeps up with releases again**

The CurseForge modpack had quietly stopped updating — it sat on v0.592.0 while the mod shipped v0.613.0, because CurseForge was accepting our uploads and then rejecting them behind the scenes with no error anywhere we could see. Uploads now retry when the platform hiccups, and every upload is checked afterwards to confirm it actually went live, so the pack can't silently fall behind again.

- CurseForge modpack is publishing again
- Failed uploads retry instead of losing that version
- A pack version that never goes live now fails loudly

### 0.617.0

**Reviewers can reply to translators, and translators can retire good AI lines**

The in-game translation editor now carries a conversation. When a reviewer turns down a translation you sent, they can say why — and that reply comes back to your client, marked against the line it is about, readable in the list and above the box when you open it, with a note on the title screen when something new is waiting. And when a machine-translated line is already correct, you can now say so: 'Good As Is' retires it from your queue so it stops coming back, and you can put it back at any time.

- Reviewers can reply to a translation, and the reply reaches the translator's client
- A title-screen note tells you when a reviewer has written back
- 'Good As Is' retires a machine-translated line that needs no fixing — reversible, and per install

### 0.616.0

**Endless Open rooms can repeat a single block variant**

An endless open portal room can now be set to repeat one block instead of the room you arrived in — an open plain of sandstone, or of a mix you build yourself. The room you walk into keeps everything its author built; only the ground stretching away from it goes uniform. The block can be a full block variant, with weights, facings and even gaps, authored in the same block-variant menu the rest of the editor uses.

- Copies: a new Single option for Endless Open rooms
- Repeat one block, or a whole block variant with weights and facings
- Air in the variant leaves gaps in the plain
- The default portal room now opens onto a lit plain of shroomlight and blackstone

### 0.615.0

**Bilibili link for Chinese-language players**

Playing in Chinese? There's now a Bilibili button on the main menu, just above Discord — Discord doesn't work in mainland China, so that one was a dead end. It only shows up on Chinese-language clients; everyone else's menu is unchanged.

- New Bilibili button on the main menu, above Discord
- Shows only on Chinese-language clients (简体中文, 繁體中文, 文言文)
- Discord stays where it is — the Bilibili link is added, not swapped in

### 0.614.0

**Portal corridor loot variety**

Chests in a portal's corridors now roll different contents from portal to portal, instead of the same ones every time.
1.21.1.0.613.0:
### 0.613.0

**Villager trade tweaks**

Adjusted what villagers pay for a few items in the Trade Anything slot.

**Player heads remember who died there**

The player heads scattered through the train are no longer anonymous. Each one now wears the face and name of a real player whose run ended at that same carriage — the fourth carriage remembers people who fell in a fourth carriage. Mine one and the head keeps them, so you can carry a fallen traveller with you or set them up somewhere of your choosing.

- Heads in carriage N show players who died at carriage N
- A mined head keeps its face and name, and can be placed anywhere
- Falls back to the bundled skins when there is nobody to remember yet
1.21.1.0.612.0:
### 0.612.0

**Using a creative mod asks first**

Using WorldEdit or Effortless Building now asks whether you want to enter Free Play, the same way switching to Creative does. Decline and nothing happens. Having them installed changes nothing on its own.

- Ordinary building with Effortless Building is still normal play

### 0.611.0

**WorldEdit available in the modpack**

The modpack now ships WorldEdit as an optional extra. It's switched off by default — tick it on in the launcher's optional-mods list if you want an in-game map editor for building. Best used off the moving train: WorldEdit's block edits aren't aware of the train's physics sub-level.

- WorldEdit bundled in the modpack, off by default
- Enable it from the optional-mods list in the CurseForge/Modrinth launcher

### 0.610.0

**Open-plain portal rooms can vary their floor**

Endless Open portal rooms can now reroll their floor and ceiling per tile instead of repeating one pattern to the horizon.

### 0.609.0

**Report a community book**

Community books written by other players now carry a report button beside the thumbs up and down. A thumbs down says a book was weak; reporting says it should not be in the pool at all. Enough reports, relative to how many people have read it, pull the book from circulation and put it in front of a human.

- A report icon sits under the thumbs on the train's question page, on player-written books only
- It takes two clicks — the first arms it, the second sends — and there is no hotkey, so a slip cannot report a book
- Reporting does not cast a vote; the two are separate verdicts
- Reports are weighed against readers, so a well-read book is not pulled by a handful of complaints

### 0.608.0

**Community books can't break your game — and can still be styled**

Books written by other players are now cleaned up before they reach you. Certain characters could previously hide text on a page or stack accent marks until it overflowed, and an emoji landing in exactly the wrong spot in a long title could crash the game outright. That's all handled now, on the server and in the mod. Colour codes and right-to-left writing still work exactly as they did — the cleanup is aimed at characters that do nothing but cause trouble. Ordinary books are unaffected.

- Colour and style codes still work in your book's pages — they're only stripped from titles and author names, where they leaked out into chat and tooltips
- Invisible padding characters are removed from titles, authors and pages; right-to-left writing and emoji sequences are left alone
- An emoji in a long title or a full page can no longer crash the game
- Books already in the community pool are cleaned as they're handed out — nothing needed re-uploading
1.21.1.0.607.0:
### 0.607.0

**Edible backpacks come from loot tables only**

Edible backpacks were being swapped into 1.5% of every loot slot in the game, on top of the chests and pots that were meant to carry them. That global substitution is gone — backpacks now turn up only where the loot tables actually list them, so finding one means something again.

- Edible backpacks no longer replace random items in unrelated containers
- Backpacks still appear in the loot chests, iron/gold chests and decorated pots that list them
1.21.1.0.606.0:
### 0.606.0

**Immediate Respawn now rolls straight into a new run**

Turn on Minecraft's Immediate Respawn game rule and dying skips the death screen entirely — the world is discarded and a fresh Dungeon Train run starts on the spot, the same reboard the death screen's "Board anew" button performs. Previously the rule dropped you back into the world you had just died in, the one way a run could outlive your death. Multiplayer is unchanged: on a server you do not host, Immediate Respawn still respawns you as vanilla does.

- Immediate Respawn ends the run and starts a new world, no button press
- Holding Shift while you die keeps the current game mode, as on the reboard chip
- Remote servers keep vanilla Immediate Respawn behaviour
1.21.1.0.605.0:
### 0.605.0

**Trade Everything is now its own download**

Trade Everything — the mod that gives every villager a "Trade Anything" slot — used to ride along inside Dungeon Train's own file. It now installs alongside Dungeon Train as its own mod, so it shows up in your mod list and gets credited for its own downloads. The CurseForge and Modrinth apps fetch it for you automatically; if you install by hand, grab Trade Everything (0.7.0 or newer) with Dungeon Train.

- The CurseForge and Modrinth apps install Trade Everything for you — nothing to do.
- Installing manually? Add Trade Everything 0.7.0+ next to Dungeon Train, or the game will tell you it's missing on launch.
- Villager payouts fixed: selling no longer hands back emerald blocks priced as ordinary goods.
- Bookshelves are now valued at 3 per emerald.
1.21.1.0.604.0:
### 0.604.0

**Difficulty changes now ask first**

Changing difficulty swaps your gear, XP and Ender Chest. It now warns you before it does — and the gear you leave behind is no longer lost.
1.21.1.0.603.0:
### 0.603.0

**Vein miner mods now trigger Free Play**

Playing with a vein miner installed runs the session in Free Play.
1.21.1.0.602.0:
### 0.602.0

**Edible backpacks are rarer**

The edible backpack turned up in almost every other chest. Its odds are now cut across the general, iron/gold and pot loot pools, and it no longer appears in the starter chest — so finding one feels like a find again.

- Edible backpack far less common in chests
- No longer handed out in the starter chest

**Miniword — a new House portal room**

Step through a portal into Miniword, a hand-built world in a box and by far the largest portal room in the game at 48x30x48. It turns up as a House room from Diff-Level 12 onward.

- New Miniword portal room — a 48x30x48 build, the biggest room in Dungeon Train
- Appears among the House portal rooms from Diff-Level 12
1.21.1.0.601.0:
### 0.601.0

**Punchy! now in the modpack (off by default)**

The Dungeon Train modpack now ships Punchy!, a first-person animation mod that adds weight and personality to swinging, mining and movement. It's included but switched off — flip it on in your launcher's mod list if you want it.

- Punchy! 2.7d bundled in both the CurseForge and Modrinth packs
- Disabled by default — enable it with one click, no extra download
- Client-side only, so it's skipped on dedicated servers
1.21.1.0.600.0:
### 0.600.0

**Nemo's Inventory Sorting available in the modpack**

The Dungeon Train modpack now offers Nemo's Inventory Sorting as an optional add-on. Turn it on in the launcher's optional-mods list to get one-click sort buttons on your inventory and any chest — handy when a loot run leaves your carriage storage a mess. It's off by default, so nothing changes unless you opt in.

- New opt-in companion mod: Nemo's Inventory Sorting (client-side, 1.8.2.1)
- Adds sort buttons to inventory and container screens
- Ships switched off — enable it in the launcher's optional mods list
1.21.1.0.599.0:
### 0.599.0

**Emerald blocks trade at their real value**

Villagers could hand you a whole emerald block (worth 9 emeralds) for a stack of cheap goods once their trade list included an emerald-block price. The Trade Anything slot now treats emerald blocks as currency rather than tradeable goods, and pays out in emeralds when a payout block would be worth more than everything you put in. Genuinely valuable items — netherite gear and the like — still pay out in blocks.

- A stack of wheat now pays out in emeralds instead of minting an emerald block.
- High-value items still pay out in emerald blocks, at nine emeralds per block.

### 0.598.0

**Shared carriages bring their furnishings with them**

A community carriage used to travel as bare blocks: the armor stands, item frames, paintings and animals someone decorated their room with were left behind when the build shipped to another world. Now they come too — a shared carriage arrives furnished, exactly as its builder left it.

- Armor stands, item frames, paintings, end crystals and mobs inside a shared carriage are saved with the build and placed back when another world receives it.
- They ride the moving train with the carriage, rather than being left standing on the tracks.
- The carriage browser's 3D preview now shows them, labelled by type and custom name, with a toggle to hide the labels.
- Server owners can cap how many travel per carriage (sharedCarriageMaxEntities, default 64) or turn the whole thing off with 0.

### 0.597.0

**Drifting carriages remember who died in them**

A drifting carriage already tells you a little about itself when you step aboard — that somebody built it, and who. It now tells you one more thing: who died in it. These are real deaths, in other people's runs, in worlds you will never see; the carriage carried the fact along with the build. A carriage nobody has died in says nothing at all, which makes the ones that do speak worth reading.

- Stepping into a drifting carriage names the travellers whose runs ended there
- The death log travels with the build, so it reaches you from other players' worlds
- Deaths by players who have not shared their name are counted, never named
1.21.1.0.596.0:
### 0.596.0

**Seven new advancements**

Three chase the bundled Edible Backpacks: eat one, craft the compressed nine-slot version, then unlock every backpack slot there is. Two reward riding past 100 and 1,000 carriages without opening a single chest or barrel (vases don't count). One is granted when you die more than 1,000 carriages into a life that never touched an ender chest. And one is for finding the train engine volume slider.

- Apples? / Hungry for Apples / Got Apples — the edible backpack chain
- Not My Chest / Still Not My Chest — 100 and 1,000 carriages without looting a chest or barrel
- Contained Loop — a 1,000+ carriage life that never opened an ender chest
- Sound Check — change the train engine volume

**Rave room**

A new carriage room stocked with music discs — the full vanilla set, occasionally worn or enchanted.

### 0.595.0

**Tectonic removed from the modpack**

The modpack no longer bundles Tectonic or Lithostitched. Dungeon Train still works with Tectonic if you install it yourself; if you had it switched on, it goes away on your next pack update.

### 0.594.0

**clientcommands counts as a cheat mod**

Playing with clientcommands installed now puts the session into Free Play.

### 0.593.0

**Three more supporter names**

Three more Discord supporters join the item name pool: mel, banguela, and morpheus the 3 feeted cat.

- Adventure Item Names 0.49.0 adds the new names — 0.48.0 still works, it just never rolls them

**Refill the Trade Anything slot with one key**

Updated the bundled Trade Everything mod. Tap space over a villager's Trade Anything slot to top it back up from your inventory instead of dragging stacks in one at a time, and obsidian now has a set trade value.

- Space-bar refill for the Trade Anything slot
- Obsidian trades at 4 per emerald
1.21.1.0.592.0:
### 0.592.0

**Edible Backpacks**

Apple packs now turn up in train loot. Eat one and you gain an extra backpack slot for the rest of your run — storage that lives in two panels either side of your inventory screen, growing a column at a time as you eat more. Golden apple packs are worth nine slots in a single bite, and nine ordinary packs craft into one. Die and the backpack goes with you, space and all, so what you carry in it is a real bet.

- Eat an apple pack for an extra inventory slot that lasts the rest of your run (up to 108)
- Storage panels sit either side of the inventory screen and hide with the recipe book
- Golden apple packs grant nine slots at once; craft one from nine ordinary packs
- Dying costs you the backpack: both its contents and the space itself
1.21.1.0.591.0:
### 0.591.0

**Sky block and portal room tweaks**

Small adjustments to sky blocks and portal rooms.

### 0.590.0

**Water and lava in carriages**

Carriages can now feature water and lava. Train builders can drop a liquid into a block variant, so a carriage might roll a flooded floor, a lava channel, or stay dry — and the liquid always arrives as a proper source block rather than a puddle that drains away.

- Water and lava can be used as block variants in carriages.
- Liquids always place as full source blocks, so they don't drain away.
1.21.1.0.589.0:
### 0.589.0

**Six player-built portal rooms**

Six new portal rooms, designed and built by players in the in-game editor — thanks to Autistic Mime, General Efficiency and Lil Detective Crunch. Which one you find depends on how far down the line you are, so the further you ride the stranger they get.

- Built by Autistic Mime, General Efficiency and Lil Detective Crunch
- Six new rooms, each gated by distance
- New loot: an End-themed chest, a gambling chest, and a mixed-blocks chest
- Their chests were rebuilt clean — the authors' worlds had baked in gear with impossible stats

### 0.588.0

**Improving dimensional carriages in the Upside Down**

Improving dimensional carriages in the Upside Down.
1.21.1.0.587.0:
### 0.587.0

**Fewer trivial runs in the passenger log**

The public passenger log now only carries runs that got somewhere. A run that ends before carriage 100 stays off the feed — whether you died, quit, or abandoned it — so the log fills with journeys instead of false starts. The one exception: if another player's echo strikes you down, your run is posted however early it happened.

- Runs ending before carriage 100 no longer post to the public passenger log
- Being killed by an echo always posts, at any carriage count
1.21.1.0.586.0:
### 0.586.0

**More skies for dimensions**

New sky options for dimensions.
1.21.1.0.585.0:
### 0.585.0

**End city adjustments**

End city adjustments.

- End city adjustments.
1.21.1.0.584.0:
### 0.584.0

**Crops saved into carriage templates stay planted**

Wheat, carrots, potatoes and beetroot saved into a carriage template no longer break the moment the carriage appears — farm carriages now ride the train intact. Crops inside a carriage no longer need light to stay planted, so an unlit farm carriage keeps its crops at the age you saved them. They still need light to grow, and still need farmland underneath: break the soil and the crop pops just like anywhere else. Also fixes saved crops vanishing from the carriage editor when you reopened a template.

- Wheat and other crops saved into carriage templates stay planted
- Crops in an unlit carriage keep their saved growth stage (they still need light to grow)
- Crops no longer vanish from a template when reopened in the carriage editor

### 0.583.0

**Drifting-carriage messages no longer flood chat**

Walking a run of drifting carriages used to fill chat with a new gray line every few seconds. Those messages are now capped at three per ten seconds, so the train still tells you when you have stepped into someone else's carriage without burying everything else you were reading.

- Drifting-carriage entry messages capped at 3 per 10 seconds

### 0.582.0

**Nether band mobs no longer spawn in dimensional carriages**

Ghasts, zombified piglins and magma cubes could spawn inside a dimensional carriage while the train crossed the Nether band. They no longer do.
1.21.1.0.581.0:
### 0.581.0

**New supporter names and the Archivist**

Twelve more Discord supporters join the item name pool, along with the Archivist Society and Archivist and Detective titles.

- Requires Adventure Item Names 0.48.0
